name: Copenhagen
title: Thickness Measurement Copenhagen | Fleet Hull Gauging
description: Ship thickness measurement for Copenhagen fleet managers: UTM for renewal surveys, CAP and ESP tank gauging, pre-docking estimates and scrubber piping.
h1: Ship Thickness Measurement and Fleet Hull Gauging for Copenhagen
intro: Greater Copenhagen is where some of the world's largest container, tanker and dry-bulk fleets are managed, and where many renewal-survey and CAP gauging programmes are decided long before a ship reaches a yard. Atlantis NDT supports Copenhagen technical managers and superintendents with ultrasonic thickness measurement on their ships — in the port itself, at Danish and Baltic docking yards, or wherever the vessel is trading — with a team mobilised from India for each job.

highlights.h: Scope set by the head office
highlights.p: Copenhagen technical departments decide renewal-survey and CAP gauging scope for ships trading worldwide. We work from your TM plan and fleet records, then send the team to the vessel, whichever port or yard it is in.

highlights.h: Short windows in the port itself
highlights.p: Product tankers at Prøvestenen, cruise ships at Oceankaj and Langelinie, and the Oslo ferry lying alongside by day all allow limited gauging, provided tank entry and cargo operations are agreed with the master beforehand.

Inside the Baltic Sea ECA, ships burn 0.10% sulphur fuel or run scrubbers. Copenhagen-managed scrubber ships need wash-water and overboard piping checked well before corrosion reaches the shell penetrations.

port.h: Copenhagen as a ship-management centre and a working port
p: Copenhagen's importance to thickness measurement comes less from the cargo crossing its quays than from the fleets run from the city and its northern suburbs. Container lines, tanker owners, dry-bulk operators, pool managers and third-party ship managers keep their technical departments here, and many of the ships they control rarely, if ever, call in Denmark. A superintendent in Hellerup or Nordhavn may be planning a third renewal survey on a Supramax docking in Asia, a CAP on a product tanker due for vetting and pre-purchase gauging on a ship a broker has shortlisted, all in the same quarter. Fleet thickness measurement for these offices is about consistency: the same TM plan conventions, the same report layout and the same approach to marking substantial corrosion, whichever yard the ship ends up in.

The port, run jointly with Malmö by Copenhagen Malmö Port, handles a narrower but useful mix. Product tankers discharge at the Prøvestenen oil harbour, cruise ships turn around at Oceankaj in Nordhavn and berth at Langelinie, and the ferry to Oslo lies alongside through the day between its overnight crossings. The Øresund carries a heavy flow of tankers, bulk carriers and container ships passing between the Baltic and the North Sea, and some of them stop in Danish waters to wait for orders, take stores or change crew.

For gauging, the useful windows in Copenhagen are short ones. A product tanker discharging at Prøvestenen will not open cargo tanks for entry, but ballast tanks, void spaces and deck structure can sometimes be measured during the stay if the master and terminal agree. Cruise ships in turnaround offer access to machinery-space piping and open decks rather than tanks. The more common pattern is that the order is placed in Copenhagen and the gauging happens at a docking yard in Denmark, Poland, Turkey or the Far East, with the Copenhagen office reviewing results each evening as the TM report builds up. That is how most Copenhagen thickness gauging work is likely to run.

facilities.h: Where gauging for Copenhagen-managed ships takes place
p: Copenhagen is not a major ship-repair port, so the measurement work that Copenhagen technical managers commission is spread across several kinds of location. Inside the port, gauging is limited to what can be done alongside: ballast tanks, deck plating, hatch coamings, piping in machinery spaces and accessible void spaces. For renewal surveys with extensive tank gauging, Danish owners usually send ships to repair yards elsewhere in Denmark or northern Europe, or schedule the docking in the region where the ship is trading so that it loses as few earning days as possible.

Within Denmark, Fayard at Munkebo on Funen and Ørskov Yard in Frederikshavn take ships for docking and repair, and the Skagen anchorage at the northern tip of Jutland is a common place for ships to wait, bunker and take stores before entering or after leaving the Baltic. Where the docking is abroad, we mobilise directly to that yard and work to the scope issued from Copenhagen; the reporting format stays the same, so results from different yards can be read side by side. Where a ship passes through the Øresund shortly before its docking, a stop off Copenhagen or Skagen can be used to measure the tanks most likely to need steel.
list: Prøvestenen oil harbour — ballast tank, deck and void-space gauging on product tankers during discharge, subject to terminal and master approval.
Oceankaj and Langelinie cruise quays — machinery-space piping, open-deck plating and accessible structure on cruise ships between turnarounds.
Ferry berths in the inner port — limited measurement on ro-pax ferries during the daytime lay-by between overnight crossings to Oslo.
Fayard, Munkebo — renewal-survey and docking gauging of cargo holds, ballast tanks and shell plating on ships routed to Funen for repair.
Ørskov Yard, Frederikshavn — docking-survey gauging and repair-scope measurement on short-sea tonnage and ferries in northern Jutland.
Skagen anchorage — pre-purchase or on-hire condition gauging of accessible spaces while ships wait off northern Jutland, with launches arranged by the agent.
Overseas docking yards — renewal and CAP gauging for Copenhagen-managed ships in Polish, Turkish or Far East yards, reported to the head-office format.

context.h: Danish flag, Baltic ECA and the regulatory picture for Copenhagen fleets
p: Denmark is a Paris MoU state, so ships calling at Copenhagen are targeted for port state control on the Paris MoU risk profile, and structural deficiencies found during an inspection — wasted ballast tank structure, holed air pipes, corroded deck fittings — often trigger the gauging request. Many Copenhagen-managed ships fly the Danish flag through the Danish International Register of Shipping (DIS). As an EU member, Denmark applies the EU ETS to shipping from 2024 and FuelEU Maritime from 2025. Emissions-driven retrofits such as energy-saving devices, shaft generators and scrubbers are often timed to coincide with a docking, so steel condition data is needed earlier to plan the whole yard stay.

Copenhagen lies inside the Baltic Sea SOx ECA, where the limit is 0.10% sulphur. Scrubber-fitted ships in fleets managed from the city therefore use their systems continuously in northern European trades, and wash-water piping, overboard lines and the shell penetrations around them see heavy service. Nordic coastal states have also been tightening rules on scrubber discharge close to their coasts, so some ships switch to compliant fuel near land and leave sections of the system idle and wet, which accelerates corrosion at steel spools, flanges and overboard penetrations. Ice is rarely an issue in the Øresund, but many Danish-managed ships trade into the northern Baltic in winter under Finnish-Swedish ice class, and their ice-belt plating deserves its own line in the TM plan.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs for Copenhagen fleets
jobs.p: Most work commissioned from Copenhagen falls into two groups: planned gauging tied to a renewal survey or CAP, and short-notice measurement after a finding by port state control, a class surveyor or a vetting inspector. Planned jobs are scoped weeks ahead with the superintendent; short-notice jobs depend on where the ship is and how quickly visas and port access can be arranged.
list: Renewal survey gauging on a Copenhagen-managed bulk carrier at its third renewal survey in a Polish yard: hold frames, topside and hopper tanks measured to the TM plan before close-up survey.
CAP thickness measurement on a product tanker approaching fifteen years, ordered by the Copenhagen office ahead of an oil-major vetting cycle and carried out during a docking.
Pre-docking gauging of ballast tanks on a container ship during a call in Danish waters, used to estimate steel renewal before the yard is contracted.
Scrubber piping inspection on a scrubber-fitted tanker: wash-water discharge lines and overboard penetrations measured alongside, with results compared against the previous docking.
Pre-purchase condition gauging of holds and ballast tanks at the Skagen anchorage for a buyer whose broker and technical team sit in Copenhagen.
A fleet thickness measurement programme covering several sister ships docking in different yards over one year, gauged and reported to a single convention.

logistics: Copenhagen Airport at Kastrup is the gateway for Copenhagen jobs and for ships at Danish yards, with onward travel by rail or road to Funen and northern Jutland. Access to Prøvestenen, the cruise quays and the ferry berths is through ISPS-controlled gates, and the ship's agent arranges gate passes against the crew or visitor list; launch boats are booked through the agent for anchorage work. Denmark is in the Schengen area, so the team travels on Schengen visas applied for in India, and we plan dates around the docking programme rather than accepting a short-notice slot we cannot reliably meet.

faqs.q: Our ships are managed from Copenhagen but rarely call in Denmark — can you still gauge them?
faqs.a: Yes, and that is the usual pattern for Copenhagen fleets. We take the scope, TM plan and previous reports from the technical department, then mobilise the team to the yard or port where the ship will be. The report follows the same format and naming conventions whichever location is used, so the superintendent can compare sister ships and successive surveys directly.

faqs.q: Can gauging be done while a tanker discharges at Prøvestenen?
faqs.a: Partly. Cargo tanks are not opened for entry during discharge, but ballast tanks, void spaces, deck plating and piping on deck can sometimes be measured if the master, the terminal and the ship's safety management system allow it. Gas-freeing and entry permits remain the ship's responsibility. Extensive cargo-tank gauging for a renewal survey or CAP belongs in a docking or a planned lay-by.

faqs.q: Does a Danish-flag (DIS) ship need anything different?
faqs.a: The measurement follows the classification society's requirements and the relevant IACS unified requirements; for a class survey, the measuring firm must hold approval from that ship's class under IACS UR Z17. The Danish Maritime Authority acts as flag state, but gauging scope is driven by class rules, the survey type and the ship's age, and we work to the TM plan agreed with the attending surveyor.

faqs.q: How far ahead should a Copenhagen office book gauging for a docking?
faqs.a: As soon as the yard slot is fixed. Our team travels from India and needs a visa for the docking country, so we need the location and dates early enough to apply and to align with the docking plan. For renewal surveys we also ask for the previous gauging report and the class TM plan, so that pre-docking estimates of steel renewal can feed into the yard specification.
